title: Water capacity constraint, independent review ordered
subtitle: Also: 2025 drinking water report endorsed, interim risk framework update, and groundwater permit request deferred to March 25.
overview: This special meeting of Regional Council was held to deal with water matters. Council directed the CAO to hire an independent third-party firm to examine how the Region reported and communicated water capacity concerns before 2026 {{vote:m2}}. The report is due within 9 to 12 months, and the review is not limited to a fixed start year. Council also endorsed the 2025 Drinking Water Summary Report {{vote:m1}}.

Staff gave two updates that were received for information, with no motions. They said sustainable operations and operational resiliency in the Mannheim service area are not expected to return until 2027. An interim risk management framework study is targeted for May 2026, and it may need more time. Staff also said the Parkway and Greenbrook plants returning to service will restore capacity rather than add new supply.

A motion asking the Province to pause new private water-taking permits in constrained areas was deferred to the March 25 meeting {{vote:m6}}. Staff are to report back on how the permit request fits provincial processes.

decisions.item: Independent review of water capacity reporting
decisions.detail: Council directed the CAO to retain an independent firm to review how water capacity concerns were identified, reported and communicated, and to report back with a timeline, findings and governance recommendations {{vote:m2}}.
Council changed the review's report-back date from six months to between nine and twelve months {{vote:m3}}.
Council removed the 2021 to 2026 timeframe so the reviewer can examine any relevant period before 2026 {{vote:m4}}.
Council endorsed the 2025 Drinking Water Summary Report, the 2025 management review of the quality management system and the infrastructure maintenance plan update {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.item: Permits to Take Water motion deferred
decisions.detail: Council deferred the request for a provincial pause on new private water-taking permits to the March 25 meeting so staff can report back {{vote:m6}}.

debate: A home builders' association delegate supported the independent review as a way to restore public confidence, and said industry is commissioning its own study of the economic costs of a prolonged development pause. The mover said the review is not about blame but about finding weaknesses in forecasting, monitoring and reporting.

Some councillors raised concerns about the review. One asked how an outside reviewer would match the expertise of staff on an unusual groundwater system. Staff said the review is about process and reporting, not technical work. Another asked about cost, and staff said it was hard to estimate before scoping and that terms could return to a closed Council meeting.

A planning consultant delegate described a freeze on building permits and urged clear risk-based rules so small projects can proceed. One councillor said planning approvals continue with holding provisions. The delegate replied that building permits are still blocked. Other councillors asked when development can receive water and whether servicing could be required at occupancy rather than at building permit.

On permits to take water, a resident delegate and the mover argued for caution given groundwater limits in the Mannheim area, and described the motion as a request to the Province. Staff cautioned that the Region will seek its own permits and that the Province may not welcome the request. Legal staff said the request is outside normal provincial process and that they knew of no similar requests.

On the 20% operational resiliency target, staff said it is evidence-based and not being revisited. The interim study will examine whether a lower level could be acceptable for a time. Councillors also pressed for clearer public messaging that Parkway and Greenbrook returning is restored capacity rather than new capacity.
